newsitem.title: GERMANY: German company earnings to grow in 1996 - Buba.
newsitem.headline: German company earnings to grow in 1996 - Buba.

text.p: German company earnings are set to grow further in 1996 on the back of an economic upswing and more moderate wage settlements, the German Bundesbank said in its monthly report on Tuesday.

The Bundesbank said the growth could lead to greater investment by companies after a period in which spending had been held back by weak demand for German products, while rising wage costs had put the emphasis on rationalisation.

"In 1996, the noticeable economic upswing and moderate development in wages should mean a further improvement in corporate earnings and a brightening of the earnings outlook..." it said in the report.
German companies had also suffered from the strong mark during the period, the central bank said, noting however that this was a factor that had "meanwhile largely been corrected."

It said that as a result of a combination of these factors the preconditions for a gain in investment activity were "more favourable". In 1995, plant investments fell two percent in gross terms, the central bank said.
Pre-tax corporate profits in 1995 rose 9.5 percent, the Bundesbank said, a noticeble slow-down compared with 1994, when profits had expanded by 28 percent against the year before.
As a whole, earnings in 1995 were some 17 percent short of those in 1991, the previous record year, it calculated.
The report noted that there were visible differences between earnings across various sectors of the German economy.
Pre-tax profits in the processing industries rose by a fifth in 1995 as the negative impact of a higher deutschemark were counterbalanced by reductions in staff numbers.
Earnings in the building sector fell by a third, marking the third year of profit decline in a row. Retail and wholesale sector profits meanwhile rose slightly.
